points.description: States that a stack is a data structure where the last item added is the first removed (last-in-first-out / LIFO), in any wording.
points.partial_credit: Half or more: gives LIFO behaviour vaguely or with a minor error (e.g. only says items are added/removed from the top without saying last in is first out).

points.description: Identifies a stack as a data structure that stores elements (a collection of items).

rubric.notes: Full marks need the LIFO property (last added is first removed) in any wording; mentioning that it is a data structure storing elements gets the last mark. Part marks for vague or slightly wrong statements of the ordering, such as "removes from the top" with no LIFO idea. Answers describing FIFO or only unrelated uses (e.g. function calls) without the LIFO property get no marks for P1.
